newsitem.title: CANADA: TransCanada to build Calgary office tower.
newsitem.headline: TransCanada to build Calgary office tower.

text.p: TransCanada PipeLines Ltd said on Friday it would build downtown Calgary's first major new office tower of the decade, adding one million square feet of office space.

TransCanada, which operates Canada's main west-east natural gas pipeline system, said it would start construction of the tower before the end of this year and planned to move in its 1,600 Calgary employees in by June 2000.

The building, with an estimated construction cost of C$150 million, was to be erected on the site of a former Greyhound Canada Transportation Corp bus terminal on 1st St. S.W. between 4th and 5th Avenues in the city's downtown core.
TransCanada spokesman David Annesley said the tower, to include office and retail space, would likely be 40 storeys tall, depending on the final design.

Downtown Calgary, home to most head offices in Canada's energy industry, experienced a massive building boom in the 1970s and early 1980s when world oil prices skyrocketed. But construction activity dried up after the oil prices fell in the late 1980s.
Office space has again become scarce with a resurgence in the country's oil and gas sector and diversification of the city's economy.

"We will need over 550,000 square feet in 2000 and expect that to increase over time to 800,000 square feet, so constructing our own building using the latest in technology appears to be an excellent solution to the problem," TransCanada chief executive George Watson said in a statement.
The company said it was conducting a worldwide search for bids for the tower's design and construction and contractor Matthews Southwest was selected to lead the development team.
